courses.title: Discovering Greeks
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Knowledge of Greek not required. Study of Greek life and culture from age of Homer to Roman conquest. Readings focus on selections from works of ancient authors in translation. Lectures illustrated with images of art, architecture, and material culture. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Requisites: courses 10, 20, at least four upper-division major courses. Limited to declared junior/senior departmental majors; minors may be admitted with consent of instructor. Topical research seminar on important themes, periods, genres of ancient Greek and Roman world. courses.title: Honors Research in Classics
courses.description: Tutorial, 15 hours. Requisite: course 198A. Limited to junior/senior departmental honors program students. Completion of final research thesis under direct supervision of faculty member. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract required. Letter grading.

Study of Roman life and culture from time of city’s legendary foundations to end of classical antiquity. Readings focus on selections from works of ancient authors in translation. courses.title: Elementary Greek
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Study of Greek Prose
courses.description: Lecture, three to four hours. Requisite: course 100. Work in sight reading and grammatical analysis of Attic prose texts; writing Attic prose. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Intensive First-Year Greek
courses.description: Lecture, 19 hours. Eight-week intensive introduction to Greek language equivalent to courses 1, 2, and 3. Offered in summer only. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Individual Studies in Greek
courses.description: Tutorial, two hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Individual intensive study, with scheduled meetings to be arranged between faculty member and student. Assigned reading and tangible evidence of mastery of subject matter required. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Directed Research in Greek
courses.description: Tutorial, two hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Supervised individual research or investigation under guidance of faculty mentor. Culminating paper or project required. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract required. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Elementary Greek
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Enforced requisite: course 1. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Intermediate Greek I
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Requisite: course 3 or 16. Formal review of Greek grammar and syntax and development of skills in reading original texts of Greek prose. Readings selected to introduce literature and culture of ancient Greece. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Elementary Greek
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Enforced requisite: course 2. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Ancient Mediterranean World
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Survey of history of ancient East from earliest times to foundation of Persian Empire. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Ancient Mediterranean World
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. History and institutions of Greeks from their arrival to death of Alexander. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History and Monuments of Ancient Greece: Field Studies
courses.description: Fieldwork, three hours. Enforced corequisite: course 112B. Examination of history, art, and monuments of ancient Greece through daily lectures and field walks to museums and archaeological sites. Part of UCLA Summer Travel Program. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Ancient Greece: Rise of Greek City-State
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Emphasis on archaic period and early classical age through Persian Wars. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Ancient Greece: Classical Period
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Clash between Athens and Sparta, consequent rise of Macedonia, and aftermath of Alexander the Great. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Rome to Death of Caesar
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Emphasis on development of imperialism and on constitutional and social struggles of late republic. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Rome from Death of Caesar to Time of Constantine
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Early empire treated in more detail, supplemented by survey of social and economic changes in 3rd century. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Rome: Transformation of Classical World
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Political, cultural, and religious history of Mediterranean in late antiquity, from crisis of Roman Empire in 3rd century to barbarian and Arab invasions and beginning of medieval states and societies in 7th century. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Topics in Ancient History
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Introduction to topics in Greek and Roman history, including Roman law, ancient Greek and Roman slavery, world of Caesar Augustus, Greek democracy, and Alexander the Great. May be repeated for maximum of 16 units with topic and/or instructor change.… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: History of Ancient Mediterranean World
courses.description: (Same as Classics M114A.) Lecture, five hours. Intensive on-site study of history and culture of ancient Rome from founding of city to conversion of Christianity. Part of UCLA Summer Travel Program. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History and Monuments of Rome: Field Studies
courses.description: (Same as Classics M114B.) Fieldwork, five hours. Enforced corequisite: course M112C. Examination of history, art, and monuments of ancient Rome through daily lectures and field walks to museums and archaeological sites. courses.title: Elementary Latin
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Study of Latin Prose
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Requisite: course 100. Work in sight reading and grammatical analysis of classical prose texts; writing of classical prose. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Individual Studies in Latin
